title: GLTF import of independent animation changes track path bone names, breaking animation
body: ### Tested versions - Reproduces in v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1], v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439] ### System information Godot v4.6.stable - macOS Sonoma (14.8.3) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M3 Max (Apple9) - Apple M3 Max (16 threads) - 64.00 GiB memory ### Issue description I'm exporting animations from blender as single GLTF files, with a single animation per file. When importing the GLTF file (containing only an Armature and a single Animation) with Save to File, and Path set in the Animation settings, the resulting Animation .tres file has the incorrect path to the bones. In the .tres it has the following: ```txt tracks/0/path = NodePath("Skeleton3D:Door_2") ``` But it should be just `Skeleton3D:Door`, not `Door_2`: ```txt tracks/0/path = NodePath("Skeleton3D:Door") ``` The armature and bones are properly named in the GLTF I know there's some retargeting logic in GLTF imports, but I don't understand why its occurring in this case. Single Armature, single Animation, no naming collisions. When the animation comes in, all of the targeted bones are suffixed with `_2`, which means the animation doesn't work without manual cleanup. ### Steps to reproduce There's a MRP with this stuff done, but here are the steps. * Create a .blend file that contains just a rig, and a single animation for that rig * Export animation track as GLTF * Double-click on the GLTF file in Godot to open the advanced import properties * Select the only animation * Enable Save to File * Set the output path to something.tres * Hit Reimport * Check the output .tres to see if the track paths are properly set ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [anim-track-path-issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25028598/anim-track-path-issue.zip)
